trigger: the sub-class blurb (roller and Hero tab)
before: You choose where the teleport squares put you, which in a dungeon is very close to owning the floor. Three illusions from day one (Mirror Self, Door Illusion and one more), and a d20 to strike until level three — let the mirror do the hitting.
after: Step on a teleport square and you choose where it puts you: any explored floor square up to 12 squares away in the eight directions, or let it choose, which in a dungeon is very close to owning the floor. Three illusions from day one (Mirror Self, Door Illusion and one more), and a d20 to strike until level three — let the mirror do the hitting.
why: IDENT-14 (report #3: "It says I choose where teleports takes me, but when I stepped on a teleport I didn't get to choose."; user ruling 2026-09-30): the blurb always promised the choice and now the engine delivers it, so the blurb says exactly what the choice is: any floor square the hero has already explored, up to 12 squares away in the eight directions, or let the teleport choose (explored squares only, user 2026-09-30). The joke about owning the floor, the three illusions and the d20 stay.

The teleporter hums and waits, the player is told how many squares glow (one square reads singular; none says the only choice is to let it choose, because only explored squares glow) and that the pick is on the map or LET IT CHOOSE. Deadpan, no rules jargon. The sample here is the plural; the singular and none variants live in the builder.
